Subject: Post-call notes + asks (SDK/auth/routing/embedding)

Thanks for the chat today — appreciate the clear demo. A short summary from my side and a prioritized list of what we need to validate before we sign: 

1) SDK/setup: we’ll be prototyping in Node (backend) and Python (embedding job). We need quickstart instructions and a short example that shows how to configure the client for private deployment (VPC) + hosted fallback.

2) Auth: primary ask is KMS-backed keys (customer-managed) + option for short-lived tokens for browser clients. We need guidance on rotation and if mTLS is required for private.

3) Routing & fallbacks: we care about latency for US users (primary) but want an automatic fallback to a lower-cost model when capacity is constrained. Can you describe rules we can control from our side?

4) Structured output & function/tool calling: for our payments workflow we plan to call 2 external services after generation (third-party CC tokenization service + internal ledger write). We want recommended patterns for tool definitions, parallel vs serial calls, and how to recover if an external tool fails mid-flow.

5) Embeddings + rerank: search relevance is the gating item. We prefer an embed-index + lightweight cross-encoder re-ranker for top-10. Need guidance on embedding batch sizes, dimensionality, and where to run reranker (hosted vs private).

6) Timeline & MAP: can we get a mutual action plan (owners, tasks, rough timeline) we can share with procurement and engineering?

Attached a one-page list of security questions procurement will ask.

Thanks,
Jules
Head of Product, Finexus

Jules — thanks, great priorities and good call. Below is a concise MAP + proposed architecture direction that maps to each of your asks. I’m keeping items scoped for a 2–3 week POC.

Summary proposals (high level):
- SDKs: we’ll provide two quickstarts (Node server + Python batch). Node will demonstrate short-lived tokens for browser + server-side key exchange; Python will show batched embedding ingestion to an S3-backed indexer. Internal owner: ben_carter.
- Auth options: support for customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-KMS) for encryption of keys at rest; short-lived JWT tokens minted by our control plane for browser flows; optional mTLS for private on-prem connections. Security doc and rotation pattern in the Drive link. Internal owner: marissa_cole (security coordination).
- Routing & fallbacks: policy-based routing exposed in our config: prefer region (us-east-1), then latency-first, then cost-fallback to quantized model variant. We expose SLO thresholds (p95 latency) and a fallback action to a cheaper model family if unmet. Configurable via API and Console.
- Function/tool calling patterns: recommend a lightweight orchestrator that accepts a single structured response from the LLM (JSON schema) with a tool manifest. Two patterns: serial (single canonical tool chain) and parallel fanout (simultaneous enrichment calls). For payments flow we recommend: 1) call tokenization tool (sync), 2) fan out enrichment calls (fraud check + metadata normalization) in parallel, 3) aggregate results with a small reconcile step. Use timeouts at call level (2000ms for external services) and a deterministic fallback policy (if tokenization fails, abort; if enrichment fails, proceed with best-effort + flag for human review). Implementation details below.
- Embeddings + rerank: plan: 1) batch embeddings (128–256 docs per job), use 1024-d vectors as default, store on vector DB with HNSW. Rerank strategy: embed + sparse retrieval to get ~100 candidates, then cross-encoder rerank top-10 on our hosted re-ranker (optionally run in private). Tradeoffs: hosted reranker gives lower ops burden; private reranker gives lower latency for high QPS.

POC MAP (2–3 weeks):
- Week 0–1: SDK quickstart (Node + Python) + auth recipe + small arch diagram (owner: ben).
- Week 1: Routing policy template + tool manifest example + sample structured output schema (owner: karthik).
- Week 2: Embedding ingestion + rerank baseline on 1k docs + error-handling tests (owner: ben + marissa).

Deliverables we’ll push to Drive: redwood-finexus-arch-v1.pdf (attached), quickstart snippets, and an Ops runbook stub.

Open Qs for you: which of the two tool-calling behaviors do you prefer as default for POC — serial canonical chain or parallel enrichment fanout? Also confirm whether your security team requires mTLS during the POC or only for full private deployment.

If that looks good I’ll draft a short SOW and calendar the kick-off.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick answers to your open Qs: 
- For the POC we prefer the parallel enrichment fanout as default: our enrichment calls (3rd-party data + internal normalizer) are independent and we want latency savings. We still want an explicit reconcile/aggregation step to handle partial failures.
- mTLS: security wants it in the long-term, but for an initial POC they are willing to accept mTLS waived if we use customer-managed KMS + strict IP allowlist.
- Reranker: please run the cross-encoder rerank hosted for the POC; we’ll evaluate moving to private if latency becomes a problem.

Next step: can you send a concrete POC task list and owners so procurement can slot the SOW? Aim to kick off next Monday.

Failure & recovery rules (short):
- Tokenization tool: transactional (no retry beyond 1 attempt); failure -> abort + manual follow-up.
- Enrichment fanout: each call has timeout 2000ms, retry up to 2 times with exponential backoff, failed enrichments marked and excluded from final payload; flag for human review.
- Model fallback: if p95 latency > configured SLO for 3 consecutive minutes, automatically route to quantized variant and log regression; hit a secondary alert to oncall.
